title: Cultivation No-Dig
stage: Back garden photographic proof for review
site: Reconstruction of a longer, reachable no-dig bed over freshly strimmed back lawn, near John's blue shed and the rear fence on its low masonry wall.

joint_render.prompt:
Three photorealistic step-by-step matched gardening photographs for John Lennon's The Vegetable Guru. Final place is JOHN'S PRIVATE CORNISH BACK GARDEN. Deliver one ultra-wide 3:1 canvas, exactly THREE equal square photos side by side with clean straight joins at 1/3 and 2/3, no gutter or text. 2172 by 724 or larger. Same one long new no-dig bed in all frames, same camera. Follow the ACTUAL domestic garden references supplied. This is a reconstruction of making a substantial new vegetable bed on lawn, not an allotment. The reader must recognise the photographed garden in the background.
References: 1 REAL camera views for John's lowered head, absolute likeness priority. 2 the previous generated triptych for ONLY face/pose/outfit in shots 1–2; the previous chin is APPROVED. Do NOT transfer that allotment, mint field shed, hedge, tall weeds, open field or tiny bed. 3 is a combined garden board: upper left REAL aerial of the compact Cornish rear garden with the blue shiplap shed beside the timber garden building and two greenhouses. Lower left shows the real low wall below the fence and existing greenhouse base. At right is an earlier book photograph demonstrating the selected garden composition: a sliver of blue shed on left, fence panels on low exposed masonry wall at rear. Use only that setting; do not import dug soil or turf piles from the digging demonstration. 4 is real hatless John in his actual checked overshirt to use in the planting photo. Ignore the greenhouse interior in this wardrobe photo.

Compose a low-key recognisable private UK rear garden, with a narrow glimpse of the real slightly weathered BLUE shed along the LEFT-hand edge in all panels. Its turquoise-blue horizontally clad wall is just visible, retain useful blue colour. Reproduce the pale weathered timber rear fence with horizontal panels and regularly spaced posts sitting on a visible low grey/buff masonry wall as in the garden reference board. The fence encloses this domestic garden; keep distant suburban sky and neighbouring buildings out of shot. The worn shed, fence and low plinth form a single continuous backdrop across each frame. Keep them quiet in top fifth of the image. A greenhouse can be outside this tight field of view. The bed and the work take centre stage. 

Critical: an amply LONG vegetable bed about 4–5 metres long by around 1.2 m wide, in proportion to this compact private garden, substantial enough to feed a family, long enough for multiple large boxes and several planting rows. It runs ALONG the garden across its formerly grassy ground, from the near foreground towards that rear fence, stopping short of the wall with a small grass strip. Camera from the path at the near end, looking along its length, so its two full long edges recede in perspective, same rectangle in all three. Show the passage beside the right edge and enough cut lawn left of the bed to see the setting. Underfoot prepare a rough but recognisable back lawn that John has ALREADY STRIMMED. Low cut grass, some green patches, pale cut stems, irregular tiny clippings tangled into the grass, a few sheared weed rosettes. No tall weeds by the bed, no meadow, no exaggerated dead hay, no pristine smooth flawless putting green. Leave underlying turf flat, unturned, unlifted. Simple unboarded bed. Show more bed than surroundings. Keep the same body scale, corner positions and visible blue shed/fence landmarks in all three shots. Same normal camera and lens. Each panel must read on its own at 45mm square. Keep hands and tools intelligibly sized in the foreground. No wide aerial viewpoint.

Likeness: prior photo likeness endorsed. In particular use supplied real 3-angle photo board to match John's lowered face: from lower lip the profile retreats markedly back toward throat; small receding chin well behind lips, very short greying beard tracing it closely; when looking down the underside foreshortens nearly into the collar. Preserve his actual nose, age, body/hand proportions and relaxed posture, no artificially strong projecting chin or extended beard. FIRST panel head at near-profile like first real face view. Same man in all photos.
LEFT, first day, soft spring light: olive knit beanie, teal fleece jacket, blue jeans and work boots. Kneeling from right grass path at the near end of the LONG plot, John overlaps a torn-open plain unprinted cardboard box panel across the previous one with a broad handspan overlap. A long run of actual overlapping flattened brown boxes extends away along the bed on the recently strimmed grass; the last short stretch is still grassy. Some real cut grass shows at the raw cardboard edges. No compost yet, no staples, no printing.
CENTRE, same session, same olive cap and teal fleece: John gently levels mature dark crumbly compost with the smooth BACK of a correctly proportioned garden rake from the path, tines upwards, centrally attached to its single long handle. Place hands naturally on shaft. Most of same long bed now has about 4 inches of rich crumbly compost; in a short unfinished stretch at far end some brown cardboard is still visible. Sloping edges. No trench.
RIGHT, one WEEK later: clearer slightly sunnier light. John now bareheaded, thinning greying hair, wearing the photographed cream/charcoal checked overshirt with rolled sleeves over dark T-shirt, blue jeans and brown shoes. No beanie and no blue fleece. Same camera/scale. Kneeling from the near grass path, with trowel in one hand and other hand easing a young lettuce plug into a small hole at same depth it grew in tray. Several small lettuce transplants, sensibly spaced in two slightly staggered rows, lead the eye back into this SAME long bed. All cardboard now covered with compost. Show the simple weathered blue shed, wall and fence in consistent position. Only a week's modest change, slight short grass regrowth. Candid UK garden photography; crisp documentary detail, no type, numbers, props from an allotment, graphic overlays, or illustrated textures.

wardrobe: Bareheaded, J01 checked overshirt and jeans
review: John approved the chin in revision 02. Location and planting outfit in this proof are new.
